hook.text: Unfinished tasks nag your mind more than completed ones. A Russian psychologist discovered this in a busy Berlin cafe.

buildup.text: Bluma Zeigarnik noticed waiters remembered unpaid orders but forgot completed ones.

discovery.text: You can harness this effect. Start a study task. Even five minutes creates an open loop that your brain wants to close.

twist.text: The hardest part is starting. Once you begin, the Zeigarnik effect pulls you back.

climax.text: Before stopping for the day, start the next section. Leave it incomplete.

punchline.text: Start it. Leave it open. Your brain will pull you back.

quiz.question: How can you use the Zeigarnik effect to overcome procrastination?
options: Complete all tasks before stopping to reduce mental load
Start a study task briefly so the open loop pulls you back to finish
Write a to-do list of all incomplete tasks each morning
